I need to figure out the secondary structure at ALA5, so I'm looking at the surrounding residues 1-12 and pulling their CA coordinates to assess backbone geometry, checking whether this stretch forms a beta strand.

Consecutive CA-CA distances all come out around 3.7-3.8 Å, consistent with a normal peptide backbone. Now I'm computing the i to i+2 distances, which fall in the 6.6-6.8 Å range -- that's characteristic of an extended beta strand conformation rather than a helix, which would show shorter ~5.5 Å distances.

I'm now checking whether this strand pairs with another nearby strand to form a beta sheet, comparing residue 5's CA position against candidate residues around position 36-38, and finding one distance (A5 to H37) close enough at ~4.4 Å to suggest possible strand pairing.

I'm also examining the 34-38 stretch for extended backbone geometry and considering whether the overall fold resembles a ferredoxin-like or Rossmann-type topology, before moving to check hydrogen bonding patterns to confirm sheet assignment.

That doesn't work either. Checking the CA-CA distances between V4/V36 and F6/S38 pairs instead, I'm getting values around 4.65-5 Å, which suggests these strands might be pairing in a roughly parallel arrangement rather than the antiparallel one I was testing.

Now I want to verify with actual hydrogen bonding patterns expected for parallel sheets, checking backbone N and O positions between residue 5 and its potential partners in the 35-36 range, but the geometry isn't lining up cleanly with any single candidate.

That doesn't work either, still too far. I'm scanning nearby atoms within roughly 5 Å of A5's position, checking V36, H37, I82, and V83, but none seem close enough to form a real contact.

Interesting though — A5 sits between H37 and I82 on either side in the z-direction, roughly 4.4 and 4.9 Å away, which suggests A5 is a central strand flanked on both sides, consistent with a parallel beta sheet. I'm now checking whether the distances between A5's oxygen and I82's nitrogen fit a hydrogen bond pattern, but the geometry comes out too far at about 4.4 Å.

Checking Y81's oxygen against A5's nitrogen gives 2.91 Å, a solid hydrogen bond, and A5's oxygen to V83's nitrogen gives 2.82 Å, another good bond — this confirms A5 forms a classic parallel β-strand pairing with N–O bonds to Y81 and O–N bonds to V83.
